## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Suniddāvimānavatthu* (Vv 26) is a canonical verse narrative located in the *Vimānavatthu* within the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. The text recounts how observing moral precepts and making alms offerings to the Noble Sangha leads to rebirth in a heavenly mansion and the attainment of great celestial happiness [SuttaCentral].

No independent parallels are recorded for the text in SuttaCentral, but computational analysis by DharmaNexus indicates extensive Pali-internal text reuse across several other *Vimānavatthu* poems as well as its commentary [DharmaNexus]. In particular, substantial formulaic verse material is shared with the *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33), the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, the immediately preceding *Niddāvimānavatthu* (Vv 25), *Soṇadinnāvimānavatthu* (Vv 23), and *Caturitthivimānavatthu* (Vv 45), along with minor correspondences in several other heavenly narrative verses [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus records low-scoring automatic alignments with a Tibetan canonical text (D 7B-2) and a Sanskrit manuscript of the *Mahāparinirvāṇasūtra*, reflecting shared stock phrases rather than curated textual parallels [DharmaNexus]. Five modern translations across five languages are indexed on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
